-- | The <a>Monad</a> class defines the basic operations over a
--   <i>monad</i>, a concept from a branch of mathematics known as
--   <i>category theory</i>. From the perspective of a Haskell programmer,
--   however, it is best to think of a monad as an <i>abstract datatype</i>
--   of actions. Haskell's <tt>do</tt> expressions provide a convenient
--   syntax for writing monadic expressions.
--   
--   Instances of <a>Monad</a> should satisfy the following:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><i>Left identity</i> <tt><a>return</a> a <a>&gt;&gt;=</a> k = k
--   a</tt></li>
--   <li><i>Right identity</i> <tt>m <a>&gt;&gt;=</a> <a>return</a> =
--   m</tt></li>
--   <li><i>Associativity</i> <tt>m <a>&gt;&gt;=</a> (\x -&gt; k x
--   <a>&gt;&gt;=</a> h) = (m <a>&gt;&gt;=</a> k) <a>&gt;&gt;=</a>
--   h</tt></li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   Furthermore, the <a>Monad</a> and <a>Applicative</a> operations should
--   relate as follows:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><pre><a>pure</a> = <a>return</a></pre></li>
--   <li><pre>m1 <a>&lt;*&gt;</a> m2 = m1 <a>&gt;&gt;=</a> (\x1 -&gt; m2
--   <a>&gt;&gt;=</a> (\x2 -&gt; <a>return</a> (x1 x2)))</pre></li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   The above laws imply:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><pre><a>fmap</a> f xs = xs <a>&gt;&gt;=</a> <a>return</a> .
--   f</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>(<a>&gt;&gt;</a>) = (<a>*&gt;</a>)</pre></li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   and that <a>pure</a> and (<a>&lt;*&gt;</a>) satisfy the applicative
--   functor laws.
--   
--   The instances of <a>Monad</a> for <a>List</a>, <a>Maybe</a> and
--   <a>IO</a> defined in the <a>Prelude</a> satisfy these laws.
class Applicative m => Monad (m :: Type -> Type)

-- | The class of monad transformers. For any monad <tt>m</tt>, the result
--   <tt>t m</tt> should also be a monad, and <a>lift</a> should be a monad
--   transformation from <tt>m</tt> to <tt>t m</tt>, i.e. it should satisfy
--   the following laws:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><pre><a>lift</a> . <a>return</a> = <a>return</a></pre></li>
--   <li><pre><a>lift</a> (m &gt;&gt;= f) = <a>lift</a> m &gt;&gt;=
--   (<a>lift</a> . f)</pre></li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   Since 0.6.0.0 and for GHC 8.6 and later, the requirement that <tt>t
--   m</tt> be a <a>Monad</a> is enforced by the implication constraint
--   <tt>forall m. <a>Monad</a> m =&gt; <a>Monad</a> (t m)</tt> enabled by
--   the <tt>QuantifiedConstraints</tt> extension.
--   
--   <h3><b>Ambiguity error with GHC 9.0 to 9.2.2</b></h3>
--   
--   These versions of GHC have a bug
--   (<a>https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/ghc/-/issues/20582</a>) which
--   causes constraints like
--   
--   <pre>
--   (MonadTrans t, forall m. Monad m =&gt; Monad (t m)) =&gt; ...
--   </pre>
--   
--   to be reported as ambiguous. For transformers 0.6 and later, this can
--   be fixed by removing the second constraint, which is implied by the
--   first.
class forall (m :: Type -> Type). Monad m => Monad t m => MonadTrans (t :: Type -> Type -> Type -> Type)
type KnownNat = KnownNat

type Bit = Bool
type W (n :: Nat) = Vec n Bit


-- | Calling Cryptol functions from ReWire programs. Unlike <a>extern</a>
--   -- a black box realized by hand-written HDL -- a <a>cryptol</a>
--   function is compiled to hardware along with the rest of the program:
--   it is present in the generated Verilog, VHDL, and Cryptol, and the
--   interpreter can evaluate it.
module ReWire.Cryptol

-- | <tt>cryptol file fn impl</tt> compiles the Cryptol function
--   <tt>fn</tt> from the Cryptol module <tt>file</tt> (resolved against
--   the importing source file's directory and the loadpath) at the type of
--   this expression, which must be monomorphic at each use site (after
--   inlining). The Cryptol module is loaded and typechecked by Cryptol
--   itself (this requires <tt>z3</tt> on the PATH), and the use-site type
--   is checked against the function's Cryptol type scheme.
--   
--   The third argument is the implementation used when the program runs
--   under GHC; rwc ignores it (the Cryptol source is the meaning). Pass
--   the definition itself if there is none:
--   
--   <pre>
--   f :: W 8 -&gt; W 8
--   f = cryptol "f.cry" "f" f
--   </pre>
--   
--   Both String arguments must be literals (after inlining).
cryptol :: String -> String -> a -> a

finite :: forall (n :: Nat). KnownNat n => Integer -> Finite n

--   unrepresentable.
toFinite :: forall (n :: Nat) (m :: Nat). KnownNat n => W m -> Finite n

maxBound :: forall (n :: Nat). KnownNat n => Finite n

--   necessary (without raising error; <tt>n</tt> must be positive, as
--   <tt><a>Finite</a> 0</tt> is uninhabited).
toFinite' :: forall (n :: Nat) (m :: Nat). KnownNat n => W m -> Finite n
fromFinite :: forall (m :: Nat) (n :: Nat). KnownNat m => Finite n -> W m

module ReWire.Bits
type Lit = W 128
zero :: Bit
one :: Bit
bit :: W 1 -> Bit

-- | The unsigned value of a bit vector, as an Integer. A GHC-only
--   convenience for simulation and testing: rwc does not compile uses of
--   this function (Integer is a compile-time-literal-only type in the
--   compiled fragment).
toInteger :: forall (n :: Nat). W n -> Integer

-- | Project range of bits. a @@ (j, i) returns bits j (most significant)
--   to i (least significant) from a (j &gt;= i). The Integer arguments
--   must be non-negative integer literals (after inlining).
(@@) :: forall (n :: Nat) (m :: Nat). (KnownNat n, KnownNat m) => W n -> (Integer, Integer) -> W m

-- | Project single bit. The Integer argument must be a non-negative
--   integer literal (after inlining).
(@.) :: forall (n :: Nat). KnownNat n => W n -> Integer -> Bit

-- | Interpret an Integer literal into a bit vector. Truncates most
--   significant bits or zero-pads to make it fit.
lit :: forall (n :: Nat). KnownNat n => Integer -> W n

-- | Resize bitvector, truncating or zero padding most significant bits.
resize :: forall (m :: Nat) (n :: Nat). KnownNat m => W n -> W m

-- | Sign-extend a bitvector by <tt>m</tt> bits (the result width is
--   inferred from the use site). Compiles to the idiomatic replicated-msb
--   concatenation.
sext :: forall (m :: Nat) (n :: Natural). KnownNat m => W (1 + n) -> W (m + (1 + n))

rOr :: forall (n :: Nat). W n -> Bit

-- | Reduction nor.
rNor :: forall (n :: Natural). W (1 + n) -> Bit

-- | Reduction xor.
rXOr :: forall (n :: Natural). W (1 + n) -> Bit

-- | Reduction xnor.
rXNor :: forall (n :: Natural). W (1 + n) -> Bit

-- | Most significant bit.
msbit :: forall (n :: Natural). W (1 + n) -> Bit

-- | Least significant bit.
odd :: forall (n :: Natural). W (1 + n) -> Bool

-- | Negation of the least significant bit.
even :: forall (n :: Natural). W (1 + n) -> Bool

module ReWire.FiniteComp
(+) :: forall (n :: Nat). KnownNat n => Finite n -> Finite n -> Finite n
(-) :: forall (n :: Nat). KnownNat n => Finite n -> Finite n -> Finite n
(*) :: forall (n :: Nat). KnownNat n => Finite n -> Finite n -> Finite n
div :: forall (n :: Nat). KnownNat n => Finite n -> Finite n -> Finite n
mod :: forall (n :: Nat). KnownNat n => Finite n -> Finite n -> Finite n
(==) :: forall (n :: Nat). Finite n -> Finite n -> Bool
(<) :: forall (n :: Nat). Finite n -> Finite n -> Bool
(<=) :: forall (n :: Nat). Finite n -> Finite n -> Bool
(>) :: forall (n :: Nat). Finite n -> Finite n -> Bool
(>=) :: forall (n :: Nat). Finite n -> Finite n -> Bool
even :: forall (n :: Nat). Finite n -> Bool
odd :: forall (n :: Nat). Finite n -> Bool

module ReWire.Interactive
type Vec (n :: Nat) a = Vector n a
class ShowHex w
xshow :: ShowHex w => w -> String
class ShowBin w
bshow :: ShowBin w => w -> String
class ShowDec w
dshow :: ShowDec w => w -> String
binary :: forall (n :: Nat). Vec n Bool -> IO ()
hex :: forall (n :: Nat). Vec n Bool -> IO ()
dec :: forall (n :: Nat). Vec n Bool -> IO ()
runIdentity :: Identity a -> a
runStateT :: StateT s m a -> s -> m (a, s)
runReacT :: ReacT i o m a -> m (Either a (o, i -> ReacT i o m a))
pretty :: Pretty a => a -> IO ()
class Pretty a
pp :: Pretty a => a -> String
type Re i s o a = ReacT i o StateT s Identity a
type RePure i o a = ReacT i o Identity a
step :: Re i s o a -> i -> s -> Either (a, s) (Re i s o a, s, o)
stepPure :: RePure i o a -> i -> Either a (RePure i o a, o)
iterRe :: (i -> Re i s o a) -> i -> s -> Either (a, s) (i -> Re i s o a, s, o)
grunt :: (i -> Re i s o a) -> (i, s, o) -> [i] -> WriterPlus (i, s, o) (Maybe (a, i, s))
run :: Re i s o a -> (i, s, o) -> [i] -> WriterPlus (i, s, o) (Maybe (a, i, s))
runP :: RePure i o a -> (i, o) -> [i] -> WriterPlus (i, o) (Maybe (a, i))
trace :: Re i s o a -> (i, s, o) -> [i] -> [(i, s, o)]
traceP :: RePure i o a -> (i, o) -> [i] -> [(i, o)]
data WriterPlus w a
(:>) :: w -> WriterPlus w a -> WriterPlus w a
(:+>) :: w -> a -> WriterPlus w a
toList :: WriterPlus w a -> [w]
instance ReWire.Interactive.Pretty GHC.Types.Bool
instance ReWire.Interactive.Pretty GHC.Num.Integer.Integer
instance ReWire.Interactive.Pretty a => ReWire.Interactive.Pretty [a]
instance ReWire.Interactive.Pretty a => ReWire.Interactive.Pretty (GHC.Internal.Maybe.Maybe a)
instance (ReWire.Interactive.Pretty a, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty b, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty c, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty d, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty e, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty f, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty g, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty h, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty i, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty j, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty k, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty l, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty m, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty n, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty o, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty p) => ReWire.Interactive.Pretty (a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, k, l, m, n, o, p)
instance (ReWire.Interactive.Pretty a, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty b) => ReWire.Interactive.Pretty (a, b)
instance (ReWire.Interactive.Pretty a, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty b, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty c) => ReWire.Interactive.Pretty (a, b, c)
instance (ReWire.Interactive.Pretty a, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty b, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty c, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty d) => ReWire.Interactive.Pretty (a, b, c, d)
instance (ReWire.Interactive.Pretty a, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty b, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty c, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty d, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty e, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty f, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty g, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty h) => ReWire.Interactive.Pretty (a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h)
instance ReWire.Interactive.Pretty ()
instance ReWire.Interactive.Pretty (Data.Vector.Sized.Vector n GHC.Types.Bool)
instance (ReWire.Interactive.Pretty w, ReWire.Interactive.Pretty a) => ReWire.Interactive.Pretty (ReWire.Interactive.WriterPlus w a)
instance ReWire.Interactive.ShowBin (ReWire.Interactive.Vec n GHC.Types.Bool)
instance ReWire.Interactive.ShowDec (ReWire.Interactive.Vec n GHC.Types.Bool)
instance ReWire.Interactive.ShowHex (ReWire.Interactive.Vec n GHC.Types.Bool)

-- | This module defines operations related to monads in ReWire, including
--   functions for defining looping monadic actions, and simplifying a
--   tower of monad transformers down to the simple ReacT action required
--   by rwc. It provides type synonyms for distinguishing looping devices
--   and stateful devices that run indefinitely.
module ReWire.Monad
iter :: (i -> o) -> i -> ReacT i o Identity ()
iterSt :: (i -> s -> (o, s)) -> i -> ReacT i o (StateT s Identity) ()

-- | Extrude a stateful device to remove the final StateT monad
--   transformer.
extrudeDev :: StateDev i o (StateT s Identity) -> s -> Dev i o

-- | Extrude a stateful device to reduce the monad transformer tower.
extrudeStateDev :: forall (m :: Type -> Type) i o s. Monad m => StateDev i o (StateT s m) -> s -> StateDev i o m

-- | Should be used to represent a looping device that operates
--   indefinitely. Formally, distinguishes a Re_+ device from an Re_INF
--   device for embedding.
type Dev i o = ReacT i o Identity ()

-- | Similar to <a>Dev</a>, but for stateful computations.
type StateDev i o (m :: Type -> Type) = ReacT i o m ()

module ReWire.Prelude
data Maybe a
Nothing :: Maybe a
Just :: a -> Maybe a
data Either a b
Left :: a -> Either a b
Right :: b -> Either a b

-- | Identity function.
id :: a -> a

-- | Constant function.
const :: a -> b -> a

-- | Function composition.
(.) :: (b -> c) -> (a -> b) -> a -> c
infixr 9 .
flip :: (a -> b -> c) -> b -> a -> c
($) :: (a -> b) -> a -> b
infixr 0 $
(&&) :: Bool -> Bool -> Bool
infixr 3 &&
(||) :: Bool -> Bool -> Bool
infixr 2 ||
not :: Bool -> Bool
otherwise :: Bool
maybe :: b -> (a -> b) -> Maybe a -> b
either :: (a -> c) -> (b -> c) -> Either a b -> c
fst :: (a, b) -> a
snd :: (a, b) -> b

-- | Converts an uncurried function to a curried function.
curry :: ((a, b) -> c) -> a -> b -> c

-- | Converts a curried function to a function on pairs.
uncurry :: (a -> b -> c) -> (a, b) -> c
undefined :: a
return :: Monad m => a -> m a
pure :: Monad m => a -> m a
(>>=) :: Monad m => m a -> (a -> m b) -> m b
infixl 1 >>=
(=<<) :: Monad m => (a -> m b) -> m a -> m b
infixr 1 =<<
(>>) :: Monad m => m a -> m b -> m b
infixl 1 >>

module ReWire.Vectors
replicate :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => a -> Vec n a
reverse :: forall (n :: Nat) a. Vec n a -> Vec n a
slice :: forall (i :: Nat) (n :: Nat) (m :: Natural) a. (KnownNat i, KnownNat n) => Proxy i -> Vec ((i + n) + m) a -> Vec n a
rslice :: forall (i :: Nat) (n :: Nat) (m :: Natural) a. (KnownNat i, KnownNat n) => Proxy i -> Vec ((i + n) + m) a -> Vec n a
index :: forall (n :: Nat) a. Vec n a -> Finite n -> a
index' :: forall (n :: Nat) (m :: Natural) a. KnownNat n => Vec ((n + m) + 1) a -> Proxy n -> a
(++) :: forall (n :: Nat) a (m :: Nat). Vec n a -> Vec m a -> Vec (n + m) a
empty :: Vec 0 a
singleton :: a -> Vec 1 a
cons :: forall a (n :: Nat). a -> Vec n a -> Vec (1 + n) a
snoc :: forall (n :: Nat) a. Vec n a -> a -> Vec (n + 1) a
head :: forall (n :: Natural) a. Vec (1 + n) a -> a
last :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => Vec n a -> a
lastIndex :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => Vec n a -> Finite n
take :: forall (n :: Nat) (m :: Natural) a. KnownNat n => Vec (n + m) a -> Vec n a
init :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => Vec (n + 1) a -> Vec n a
drop :: forall (m :: Nat) (n :: Natural) a. KnownNat m => Vec (n + m) a -> Vec m a
tail :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => Vec (1 + n) a -> Vec n a
update :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => Vec n a -> Finite n -> a -> Vec n a
map :: forall a b (n :: Nat). (a -> b) -> Vec n a -> Vec n b
generate :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => (Finite n -> a) -> Vec n a

-- | Returns evens from v concatenated with evens from w
packlo :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => Vec n a -> Vec n a -> Vec n a

-- | Returns odds from v concatenated with odds from w
packhi :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => Vec n a -> Vec n a -> Vec n a

-- | Returns the first half of v interleaved with the first half of w
unpacklo :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => Vec n a -> Vec n a -> Vec n a

-- | Returns the second half of v interleaved with the second half of w
unpackhi :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => Vec n a -> Vec n a -> Vec n a

-- | lookup value at index n in vector
(!) :: forall (n :: Nat) (m :: Natural) a. KnownNat n => Vec ((n + m) + 1) a -> Proxy n -> a
infixl 9 !

-- | assign new value a to index i
(!=) :: forall (n :: Nat) a. KnownNat n => Vec n a -> Finite n -> a -> Vec n a
infixr 2 !=
